newsitem.title: USA: IBP says short supplies of meat halved its profits.
newsitem.headline: IBP says short supplies of meat halved its profits.

text.p: IBP Inc., one of the world's largest producers of beef, pork and meat products, said Thursday that "challenging market conditions," including tight supplies of cattle and hogs, cut its profits in half in the third quarter.
The giant meat processor said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 plunged to $40.5 million, or 42 cents a share, from $85.4 million, or 88 cents a share, a year ago.

The company, which is based Dakota City, Neb., said its overall sales slipped to $3.18 billion from $3.29 billion -- with the recent outbreak of food poisoning in Japan accounting for some of the decline.
"As the outbreak ends and these concerns subside, we believe shipments to Japan will return to more normal levels," the company said.

IBP, which supplies fresh beef, pork and prepared meats for the retail and food service industries, said that for the first nine months of the year its net income fell to $180.5 million, or $1.87 a share, from $223.1 million, or $2.31 a share.
Net sales for the nine months were flat at $9.5 billion, the company said.
IBP also said that Martin Massengale, president emeritus of the University of Nebraska, who has an extensive background in education and agriculture, was joining the company's board.
IBP's stock added 25 cents to $24.125 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
